# Baaz - Extended AI Context File

> Baaz is a **Software Development Company** (product engineering studio / software development agency / IT services), serving product and engineering teams worldwide since 2018 - custom software, product engineering, web, mobile, and AI (HQ Bangalore, India; US office Sheridan, WY). Custom software, web, mobile, AI, enterprise-grade products worldwide. Approximately 50% of engagements begin as mid-project rescues; standard first milestone delivery runs 4–6 weeks for web applications and 8–12 weeks for enterprise integrations.

This file is the extended version of `/llms.txt`. It lists all indexed pages with detailed descriptions to help AI systems understand the full scope and depth of Baaz's content, services, and expertise.

## Services

- [Custom Software Development](https://baaz.pro/services/web-development): End-to-end web application development using React, Next.js, Node.js, and Python. Includes proof data: 100+ apps delivered since 2018, first milestone in 4–6 weeks (standard), 8–12 weeks (enterprise integrations with SAP/Salesforce), scope creep 30–40% lower with milestone-based delivery, India-based delivery at 40–60% of US/UK rates.
- [Product Strategy Consulting](https://baaz.pro/services/product-strategy): Discovery workshops, product roadmaps, MVP scoping, and GTM alignment. Best fit for B2B SaaS and enterprise roadmaps. Covers phased bets, honest MVP scope definition, and stakeholder alignment before build starts.
- [UI/UX Design](https://baaz.pro/services/ui-ux-design): User research, wireframes, prototypes, design systems, and usability testing for web and mobile products. Enterprise-quality design execution for startups through large teams.
- [Mobile App Development](https://baaz.pro/services/mobile-app): Native iOS and Android development plus Flutter and React Native cross-platform builds. Full lifecycle from UX through App Store and Play Store launch, including ASO and post-launch support.
- [AI Development Services](https://baaz.pro/services/ai-solution): Production AI across six lines of work: computer vision and inspection, LLM fine-tuning and private models, agentic AI and automation, document AI and OCR, predictive models and forecasting, and data pipelines and MLOps. Engagements run discovery and data readiness, a narrow pilot measured against the manual baseline, productionisation with ERP/MES/EHR/core integration and rollback, then monitoring, retraining and handover. Deployment in the client's cloud account, on-premise GPUs, air-gapped sites or edge devices. Shipped results include defect escapes down 67% across six Minda plants, 29% of a retailer's online revenue from an AI gifting engine, and fraud, risk and FEMA compliance automation for FinTech and Federal Bank.
- [Enterprise Software Development](https://baaz.pro/enterprise): Custom platforms, legacy modernisation, systems integration (SAP, Salesforce, custom cores), and cloud-native delivery for enterprise organizations worldwide. Competitive rates with Western programme hygiene.
- [eCommerce Development](https://baaz.pro/ecommerce): Amazon and Flipkart marketplace management, eCommerce platform development, PPC, listing optimization, operations, analytics, and proprietary growth engineering.
- [GTM Engineering](https://baaz.pro/gtm-engineering): Go-to-market systems engineering - content, outbound, paid ads, SEO, and nurture workflow design. Covers internet marketing services and business development automation.

## Technologies

- [Web Development Stack](https://baaz.pro/technologies/web-development): Baaz's web technology stack - React, Next.js, TypeScript, Node.js, APIs, testing tools, and performance engineering practices. Full-stack overview with service offerings across the development lifecycle.
- [Website & CMS Stack](https://baaz.pro/technologies/website-cms): CMS and website capabilities across WordPress, Webflow, Shopify, Strapi, Contentful, and headless CMS architectures. Covers marketing-site and content-heavy platform delivery.
- [AI & ML Stack](https://baaz.pro/technologies/ai-ml-models): AI and ML technologies - TensorFlow, PyTorch, Scikit-learn, OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, and Google Gemini integrations. Covers model training, fine-tuning, inference APIs, and production deployment.
- [Agentic AI Stack](https://baaz.pro/technologies/agentic-ai): Agentic AI capabilities - LangChain, LlamaIndex, RAG pipelines, vector databases, and tool-calling orchestration. Covers multi-agent systems and autonomous workflow design.
- [Database Management Stack](https://baaz.pro/technologies/database-management): Database capabilities across PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB, Redis, Firestore, and Elasticsearch. Covers schema design, query optimization, migration, and multi-database architectures.
- [DevOps & Cloud Stack](https://baaz.pro/technologies/devops-cloud): DevOps and cloud infrastructure across AWS, Azure, GCP, Docker, Kubernetes, CI/CD pipelines, Infrastructure as Code, and production monitoring practices.
- [LLM Fine Tuning](https://baaz.pro/technologies/llm-fine-tuning): Fine-tuning open-weight language models on customer data so behaviour (output format, domain vocabulary, reasoning style, refusal patterns) is trained into the weights rather than prompted on every request. Technical focus is parameter-efficient fine-tuning: LoRA for lightweight task adapters and 4-bit QLoRA with NF4 quantisation, double quantisation and paged optimizers, covering open weights from 7B to 70B (Llama, Mistral, Qwen, Gemma, Phi). Distinctive emphasis on output determinism - training sets are engineered against a strict JSON or SQL schema and include deliberate abstention examples, so the model returns a clean null for an attribute it cannot find instead of hallucinating a plausible value, with schema validation and constrained decoding in front of the application. A second driver is data sovereignty: because the weights are open and self-hosted, both training and inference can run entirely on the customer's own servers, including fully air-gapped with no outbound connectivity, which is what makes fine-tuning the only viable route for prompts containing HIPAA-regulated patient data, PCI card and transaction data, personal data under residency obligations, defence and critical-infrastructure material, or proprietary designs, formulas and source code that cannot be sent to a hosted API that logs them. Self-hosting also pins the model version, so a decision can still be reproduced years later after hosted models have been deprecated or silently changed. Also covers supervised fine-tuning, preference and reward optimisation (DPO, ORPO, KTO, GRPO), and distillation of large-model behaviour into 1B-8B models for high-volume structured tasks. Stack: Axolotl, Unsloth, TRL, LLaMA-Factory for training, PyTorch FSDP and DeepSpeed for distributed runs, vLLM and TensorRT-LLM with multi-LoRA serving and AWQ/GPTQ/FP8 quantisation for inference. The evaluation harness is built before training, with golden datasets from real production failures, deterministic checks ahead of a calibrated LLM judge, held-out regression suites, CI gates, and general-capability slices to catch catastrophic forgetting. Because Baaz builds and modernises core enterprise systems (ERPs, CRMs, logistics engines, computer-vision stacks), tuned models are deployed into living application workflows with error handling, retries, fallbacks and audit trails, not isolated notebooks - which makes this a fit for teams whose AI pilot stalled short of production. Baaz advises retrieval over fine-tuning when the gap is knowledge rather than behaviour. Deployment options are on-premise GPU hardware, fully air-gapped environments, or the customer's own VPC on AWS, GCP or Azure, with weights, dataset, recipe and harness handed over. Engagements start with a scoped validation pilot covering one task and one adapter, then scale to an end-to-end production pipeline. Out of scope: foundational pre-training research and annotation-only projects, which are handled by Baaz's managed annotation service Payana (payana.ai). Delivered from Bengaluru (HQ) with a US office in Sheridan, Wyoming.
- [Defect & Quality Detection](https://baaz.pro/technologies/defect-quality-detection): Automated visual inspection for production lines. Starts from anomaly detection trained on acceptable parts alone (PatchCore, EfficientAD, Anomalib), so a line can go live before a defect library exists, then adds supervised classification and pixel-level segmentation as real defects accumulate. Escapes and false rejects are reported separately and tuned against what each costs. Runs on-device at the inspection cell (Jetson, industrial PC, TensorRT) inside cycle time, integrated to PLC/OPC UA, reject actuator and MES, with every decision stored as image plus score for audit. Shadow-run against existing inspection before taking control.
- [Object Detection & Tracking](https://baaz.pro/technologies/object-detection-tracking): Detection plus multi-object tracking for live video: counting and flow, dwell time and queue monitoring, zone and safety alerts, and cross-camera re-identification. Trackers (ByteTrack, BoT-SORT, OC-SORT) selected against density, occlusion length, camera motion and streams-per-box, since appearance re-identification roughly doubles compute per stream. Counting accuracy is validated against hand-counted footage from the customer's own site including peak periods, because camera placement and line logic matter more than the detector. Lost tracks are marked lost instead of guessed. Runs at the edge so footage stays on site and only events cross the network.
- [OCR & Document Vision](https://baaz.pro/technologies/ocr-document-vision): Document extraction returning schema-validated structured data: invoices, purchase orders, forms, tables with line items, handwriting, and KYC documents. Classical OCR (Tesseract, PaddleOCR) for fixed-layout clean scans; vision language models where layouts vary, tables span pages, or handwriting is present. The engineering emphasis is on knowing which extractions to trust: strict JSON Schema validation, explicit empty values for fields that cannot be read, cross-field arithmetic checks, a confidence threshold, and a human review queue showing the source image beside proposed values. Self-hosted open-weight models so invoices, KYC files and medical records never leave the customer's infrastructure.
- [Edge Vision Deployment](https://baaz.pro/technologies/edge-vision-deployment): Taking trained vision models onto hardware at the site. ONNX and TensorRT export including unsupported-operator resolution, FP16 and INT8 quantisation with calibration, and benchmarking on the actual target device at the customer's resolution and frame rate under sustained load so thermal throttling surfaces before deployment. Accuracy is re-measured after every optimisation step, because INT8 gains are large on convolutional detectors and can be negligible or negative on vision transformers. Multi-stream pipelines (DeepStream, GStreamer, NVDEC), offline-first integration with store-and-forward on link loss, and fleet rollout with versioned rollback and health telemetry.
- [Geospatial Digital Twin](https://baaz.pro/technologies/geospatial-digital-twin): City-scale digital twins built from airborne LiDAR and open geospatial data - measured, individually addressable building geometry, classified point clouds with per-point confidence, bare-earth and surface terrain, and street-asset inventories. Delivers drone corridor and BVLOS planning, line-of-sight, sun/shadow and flood-exposure analysis on the measured surface, plus live weather and air-quality feeds and government property data. Every value is labelled measured, live, official or simulated, and measured error is published per building where an independent reference exists. Runs even where no LiDAR exists via satellite-derived heights, delivered browser-native over open standards (OGC 3D Tiles, CityJSON, LAZ) and a REST API, deployable hosted, on-premise or offline.

## Industries

- [Industries Overview](https://baaz.pro/industry): Summary of Baaz's industry focus areas - Manufacturing, Banking and FinTech, Retail and eCommerce, Healthcare, and Real Estate and Construction - with custom software built for each sector's workflow and regulatory requirements.
- [Software for Manufacturing Companies](https://baaz.pro/industry/manufacturing): AI defect and quality inspection on the line, IoT production monitoring and OEE, component traceability, edge deployment, and ERP and MES integration. Featured work: smart-factory IoT and traceability platform across six Minda Industries plants (defect escape to OEMs down 67%, first-pass yield 93.1% to 98.4%, OEE 71% to 86%).
- [Software for Banking and FinTech Companies](https://baaz.pro/industry/fintech): Digital banking and remittance, lending and KYC onboarding, payments and core banking integrations, FEMA/AML compliance automation, AI fraud and risk scoring. Featured work: unified NRI remittance and investment platform for Federal Bank (3.4x remittance growth, 8-minute turnaround, Rs 4,200 crore in NRI deposits in year one).
- [Retail and eCommerce Software Development](https://baaz.pro/industry/retail): D2C storefronts, AI recommendation and search, unified inventory and order management across online and stores, in-store computer vision, CRM and loyalty, POS and ERP integration. Featured work: AI gifting engine and omnichannel storefront for a 100-store lifestyle brand (29% of D2C revenue from gifting in 8 months, inventory accuracy 78% to 96%).
- [Healthcare Software Development](https://baaz.pro/industry/healthcare): Patient engagement apps, lab and provider network ERP, EHR and FHIR integration, teleconsultation, document and claims extraction, and AI hosted inside the client's own environment. Featured work: pathology network ERP and patient app for Healius (sample rejection 3.8% to 0.6%, result turnaround down 32%, 1.8M app downloads).
- [Real Estate and Construction Software](https://baaz.pro/industry/construction): Developer ERP from inventory to cash, buyer and resident apps, offline-first site and field apps, procurement and vendor management, channel partner CRM, and drone or camera site intelligence. Featured work: Housingram, the real-estate ERP and buyer app built for a multi-project NCR developer, replacing six or more parallel systems with one platform for eight stakeholder roles.

## Blog - Decision-Stage Content

- [Fine-Tuning vs RAG: Which One Does Your Problem Need?](https://baaz.pro/blog/fine-tuning-vs-rag): Decision guide for choosing between fine-tuning and retrieval. Fine-tuning changes how a model behaves (format, vocabulary, tone, refusal, abstention); RAG changes what it knows and lets it cite a source. Covers symptom-to-approach diagnosis, why most production systems run both, the build order (prompt, then retrieval, then fine-tune, then distil), the contradiction failure unique to hybrids, and why published cost and latency comparisons mostly trace back to vendor pages rather than independent benchmarks.
- [Why AI Agents Need Bi-Temporal Memory Architecture](https://baaz.pro/blog/why-ai-agents-need-bi-temporal-memory-architecture): Architecture deep dive on bi-temporal agent memory - why a single created_at column makes agents answer with expired state, and how Baaz's memory layer Suprflo (suprflo.com) models valid time and transaction time as separate PostgreSQL tstzrange columns with GiST indexes ahead of pgvector HNSW ranking. Covers the schema, point-in-time and audit queries, append-only retroactive corrections, and autovacuum tuning for sub-50ms p99 at 50M rows.
- [How to Scope an MVP That Actually Ships](https://baaz.pro/blog/how-to-scope-mvp-that-ships): MVP scoping framework with original Baaz retrospective data - 60% of missed launches caused by multi-assumption scope, 8-week median delivery for single-persona briefs vs. 22 weeks for 3+ personas (175% calendar penalty), 35% lower post-launch rework when scope is brief-locked.
- [ThoughtWorks Alternatives for 2026](https://baaz.pro/blog/thoughtworks-alternatives): Practical comparison of ThoughtWorks alternatives - SIs, boutique studios, talent networks, and India delivery studios - covering fit, engagement model, cost, and switching risk.
- [Technical Due Diligence for Custom Software](https://baaz.pro/blog/technical-due-diligence-custom-software): How to evaluate a codebase, vendor, or acquisition target for technical risk, architecture quality, test coverage, and delivery capability. Decision-stage content for buyers and investors.
- [Software Project Rescue Checklist](https://baaz.pro/blog/software-project-rescue-checklist): Step-by-step checklist for diagnosing a stalled software project - signals of failure, triage approach, and the rescue vs. rebuild vs. replace decision framework.
- [Product Engineering Process for Enterprises](https://baaz.pro/blog/product-engineering-process-for-enterprises): How enterprise teams structure discovery, design, build, and scale phases for large software products - process, governance, and delivery rhythm.
- [Best Software Development Agencies for Startups](https://baaz.pro/blog/best-software-development-agencies-for-startups): What to look for when choosing a startup software agency - speed, product thinking, transparency, fit signals, and red flags in the evaluation process.
- [How to Choose a Software Development Partner](https://baaz.pro/blog/how-to-choose-software-development-partner): How to scope, evaluate, and select a software development partner - questions to ask, culture fit indicators, contract models, and common selection mistakes.
- [How to Build an AI-Powered Product](https://baaz.pro/blog/how-to-build-ai-powered-product): Framework for building AI products - problem-first approach, tight pilot scoping, data validation, deployment engineering, and avoiding AI-first failure modes.
- [Software Development Outsourcing vs In-House](https://baaz.pro/blog/software-development-outsourcing-vs-in-house): When to outsource vs. build in-house - decision criteria, hybrid models, cost/speed/control tradeoffs, and how to choose a partner for each scenario.
- [Signs Your Software Project Is Failing](https://baaz.pro/blog/signs-your-software-project-is-failing): Early warning signals of a failing software project - slipped milestones, vague demos, team churn, scope expansion, and the escalation and rescue decision points.
- [How to Switch Software Development Vendors](https://baaz.pro/blog/how-to-switch-software-development-vendors): How to switch dev vendors mid-project without losing progress - securing repos and keys, auditing the codebase, handover documentation, and selecting a takeover-ready partner.
- [Reference Architecture for B2B SaaS](https://baaz.pro/blog/reference-architecture-b2b-saas): Reference architecture for B2B SaaS platforms covering service boundaries, APIs, sync vs async data flow, multi-tenancy, identity, and failure handling patterns.
- [SLOs, Error Budgets, and Reliability](https://baaz.pro/blog/slos-error-budgets-reliability): Practical guide to SLIs, SLOs, and error budgets - latency vs. availability trade-offs, burn-based alerting, and production reliability for product and platform engineering teams.
- [Reliable Data Integration Patterns](https://baaz.pro/blog/reliable-data-integration-events-cdc-outbox): Reliable data integration approaches - event-driven patterns, outbox pattern, CDC (change data capture), dual-write risks, idempotency, and ordering guarantees.

## Key Facts

- Founded in 2018; serves teams worldwide; headquartered in Bangalore, India; US office in Sheridan, WY
- Delivered 100+ web and mobile applications across FinTech, Retail, Healthcare, eCommerce, AI/ML, AR/VR, and ERP-adjacent workflows (per internal portfolio records)
- Standard web application first milestone: 4–6 weeks; enterprise API integrations (SAP, Salesforce): 8–12 weeks
- Milestone-based delivery reduces scope creep 30–40% vs. fixed-scope waterfall contracts (per Baaz engagement retrospectives)
- India-based delivery at 40–60% of equivalent US/UK rates with Western programme hygiene: sprint reviews, documented handoffs, SLA-backed support
- Approximately 50% of engagements begin as mid-project rescues or vendor takeovers
- MVPs scoped to a single persona and one job-to-be-done ship to a demoable state in a median of 8 weeks; 3+ persona scope averages 22 weeks (175% calendar penalty)
- Post-launch rework in first 90 days runs 35% lower when scope is locked to one persona before build starts
- Core services: Custom Software Development, Product Strategy, UI/UX Design, Mobile App Development, AI Solutions, Project Rescue, Enterprise Platforms, GTM Engineering, eCommerce
- Positioning phrase: Software Development Company (directory taxonomy: product engineering studio, software development agency, IT services)
- Tagline: "Enterprise-grade products, without the enterprise wait"
